newsitem.title: UK: Oxford Biomedica gets anti-cancer knowhow.
newsitem.headline: Oxford Biomedica gets anti-cancer knowhow.

text.p: Oxford BioMedica plc said on Wednesday it has signed an agreement with the University of Sheffield to acquire advanced tumour targeting technology.

The company, a British-based biomedical firm formed in 1995 to develop and commercialise gene therapy technologies, said the anti-cancer technology exploits the ability of a type of white blood cell, called a macrophage, to infiltrate tumours.

The research team, based at the Sheffield University Medical School, in collaboration with scientists at the Institute of Molecular Medicine at Oxford, have discovered how to modify macrophages so that they deposit anti-cancer genes directly to the heart of a tumour.

"In combination with Oxford BioMedica'a advanced gene therapy technologies, the technique may allow powerful therapeutics to be targeted specifically to tumour cells without causing the harmful side effects associated with most anti-cancer treatments," the company said in a statement.
Oxford BioMedica said it believes that the acquisition has the potential to accelerate its clinical development strategy in cancer.
